strategy.headline: Indiana is where the game lives, and this season the NBA brings its Cup final to Hinkle.
strategy.thesis: Pacers fandom is a statewide faith, born in county-seat gyms and Hinkle Fieldhouse. The team belongs to Indiana, not just Indianapolis, and its navy and gold echo the gold torch on the state flag's blue. 2026-27 hands Nike a rare stage: the 2025 Finals core comes home after a 19-63 lost year, with Haliburton healthy. And the Emirates NBA Cup final comes to Hinkle on Dec 11, whether or not the Pacers play in it. The comeback is the fans' story, so tell it team-first. Use the Fieldhouse, the franchise's ABA archive, Attucks '55 and Indiana Avenue, and a name taken from both the Indy 500 pace car and harness-racing pacers. The buyer is value-led, cold-weather and mall-first, so Pacers-licensed heavyweight layers and statewide distribution matter as much as any limited drop.

archetype.name: The Keepers of the Gym
archetype.description: Fans raised on a single-class state tournament that ran until 1997, on county gyms that out-seat their towns and on Hinkle's 1928 barrel vault. They reward effort over flash, and their navy and gold is Pacers loyalty that travels from Mass Ave to New Castle.

pulse.teamMoment: Tyrese Haliburton is back from the Achilles tear he suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 Finals. After a 19-63 season, he rejoins Siakam, Nembhard, Nesmith, McConnell and deadline pickup Ivica Zubac under Rick Carlisle. Kelly Oubre Jr., Larry Nance Jr. and two-way Purdue guard Braden Smith join them. Indiana hosts the 76ers on the Oct 30 opening Cup Night and has no opening-night or Christmas Day game.
pulse.sentiment: Cautiously hopeful and protective. Fans expect a bounce-back toward contention, but they remember how fast the 2025 high ended. They will punish anything that feels like hype or exploits the injury.

topInsights.title: Dec 11 at Hinkle is Indiana's night, with or without the Pacers
topInsights.insight: The Cup final moves from Las Vegas to Hinkle, the 1928 barn where Milan won in 1954 and state finals were played through 1971. Locally, that reads as the league honoring Indiana's basketball home. Gym-hoppers, college fans and Pacers diehards all treat Hinkle as shared ground, so the night is bigger than one team's result.
topInsights.implication: Build a Pacers-licensed winter capsule (maple, navy, truss-arch geometry, 92-county graphics) that sells from Nov 1 with no Hinkle or Cup mark. Add a Hinkle-named layer only if Butler and the NBA clear it by mid-October.

topInsights.title: The comeback belongs to the whole team
topInsights.insight: Haliburton's return is the season's emotional center. But fans are protective of the injury and wary of a manufactured star push, and he has been a Puma footwear athlete since October 2024. The story Nike can tell in full is the 2025 Finals core back together, in the Fieldhouse it shares with the Fever.
topInsights.implication: Launch a plain "Home" team lockup carrying the core and the Fieldhouse, with no player name or injury imagery. Lead player product with NBA-licensed swingman and youth jerseys, released once Haliburton has played a home game.

topInsights.title: Sell to 92 counties, not one skyline
topInsights.insight: The fan base runs from 317 out to 765 and 812 towns whose gyms out-seat their populations. Volume sells at suburban malls, the Edinburgh outlets, Lids and Finish Line, not a downtown flagship. The edges split: the Region leans Chicago, the south leans Kentucky, and IU-versus-Purdue divides households.
topInsights.implication: Anchor county-number product (49 for Marion County, 765, 812) under the Pacers wordmark. Sell it through an embroidery and patch bar at the Fieldhouse store and a few Lids doors. Keep IU, Purdue, Notre Dame and Butler color pairings off it.

topInsights.title: Attucks '55 and Indiana Avenue are the market's unspent story
topInsights.insight: Oscar Robertson's Crispus Attucks Tigers won the 1955 and 1956 state titles a few blocks from the Avenue clubs where Wes Montgomery and Freddie Hubbard played. Then highways and campus expansion cleared the neighborhood. The white small-town Hoosiers myth has long crowded the story out, and no Pacers City Edition has told it.
topInsights.implication: Release a heritage collection in boys' state-finals week, the anniversary window of the 1955 title. A paid Black Indianapolis design lead authors it, with the Madam Walker Legacy Center and the Crispus Attucks Museum under written consent. Plan the calendar around a possible no.

topInsights.title: ABA titles and "Boom Baby": an under-mined archive
topInsights.insight: The Pacers won ABA titles in 1970, 1972 and 1973 with Roger Brown, two-time MVP Mel Daniels and coach Bobby "Slick" Leonard. Leonard's "Boom Baby!" call is the market's best-loved catchphrase. The returning Moments Mixtape already prints it on the anthem tag, so the archive is live in the uniform.
topInsights.implication: Extend the Mixtape into the ABA archive: blue-and-gold era lettering, title-year numerals and a two-word "Boom Baby" callout credited to Leonard's estate and the Pacers. Use red-white-blue ABA-ball cues only as trim, and clear them with the league.

topInsights.title: The Pacers are the last team to knock out the champions
topInsights.insight: Indiana beat New York in the 2025 East finals, and the Knicks went on to win the 2026 title. So the rivalry of Reggie's 8.9 seconds has a fresh line: the last series New York lost was to the Pacers. The two meet in Cup Group B.
topInsights.implication: Tell it in dates and numerals ("8.9", "5.7.95", the 2025 series clinch date) in bulb-scoreboard type. No likeness, taunt or gesture graphics.

topInsights.title: The season is lived in cold gyms on a Midwest budget
topInsights.insight: Basketball fills Indiana's gray November-to-March half-year of overheated gyms and letter jackets. Shoppers pay a flat 7% sales tax with no tax holiday, so promotions, bundles and youth sizes drive the base. Tees and hoodies outsell jerseys. Haliburton leads youth demand, and Reggie's 31 is the heritage gift.
topInsights.implication: Lead the in-season assortment with heavyweight fleece, quarter-zips and beanies at a strong entry price. Add a clear step-down below Swingman and a small premium layer.

uniform.concept: Attucks '55: The Avenue. Proposed for the 2027-28 City Edition slot if it's open, otherwise a heritage or Classic lane.
uniform.narrative: In 1955 Crispus Attucks, the city's segregated Black high school, won the state with Oscar Robertson. The school sat a few blocks from the Indiana Avenue clubs of Wes Montgomery and Freddie Hubbard, and the city sent its celebration away from Monument Circle. A uniform authored with the Crispus Attucks Museum, the Madam Walker Legacy Center and a Black Indianapolis design lead gives the city the founding story the Hoosiers myth crowded out. The rest of the state learns its own history.
motifs: An abstract double pinstripe down the side panel, a nod to the Avenue's jazz without naming any artist
Stepped terra-cotta border on the trim, drawn by partner artists from the Walker building only with the Center's written consent
The Indiana flag's torch and stars at the back neck
uniform.typography: A custom chest wordmark drawn by the Black Indianapolis design lead. Navy block numerals outlined in brass keep TV legibility on the terra-cotta field. Test the contrast early.
details: Navy shorts and navy-and-gold trim so the set still reads Pacers
Jock tag credits the co-design partners by name
Neck tape reads 1955 and 1956 for the two titles, including the unbeaten '56 team
Court tie-in: terra-cotta lane paint and an Avenue map at the baseline, unveiled in state-finals week
avoid: Repeating verified past City Editions: 2019-20's racing "Always Lead", the hand-scripted "Indy" sets of 2023-25 and the 2025-27 Moments Mixtape. Check Classic and Statement history too.
Brass numerals directly on terra cotta (weak contrast)
Segregation-era imagery, Jim Crow signage or the Walker building's ornament used as decoration
Oscar Robertson's name or likeness without his participation and license, or Attucks school marks without written permission
A literal checkered flag, Hoosiers-film Hickory marks, Robert Indiana's LOVE lettering, or Butler blue, IU crimson, Purdue old gold and Notre Dame navy-gold pairings

scorecard.rationale: A Hinkle Cup final and Haliburton's return give a small market near-average opportunity and above-average gym-faith fandom. Value-led, mall-first retail with no destination door sits in the bottom tier (brief scores: opportunity 68, culture 76, retail 45, fandom 72). Indiana has one of the league's deepest basketball cultures and a one-off Hinkle Cup final in a comeback season. That lifts opportunity above average despite a small market. Retail sits below average: no destination flagship, a mall-first, value-led buyer, a star with a rival footwear deal and major cues that need third-party clearance.

Partner status: Music for All and ISSMA November 2026 dates, Catch the Stars Foundation, People for Urban Progress, Plump's Last Shot, 2027 Indy 500 date.

music.headline: Indy's sound is brass and heritage, and the Pacers already have the soundtrack.
music.summary: Indianapolis music runs on heritage and brass. The Indiana Avenue jazz clubs sat a few blocks from Oscar Robertson's Crispus Attucks title teams, and the city is now the center of American marching music. Its real anthem is a 1917 song, "Back Home Again in Indiana." This season the sound fits Haliburton's return and the white, royal blue and gold Moments Mixtape City Edition.

insights.title: Jazz and basketball shared the Avenue
insights.detail: In the 1940s and 50s, Indiana Avenue's clubs produced Wes Montgomery, Freddie Hubbard, J.J. Johnson and David Baker. A few blocks away, Oscar Robertson's Crispus Attucks Tigers won the 1955 and 1956 state titles, the first all-Black school in the nation to win an open state championship. Highways and the IUPUI campus later cleared much of the neighborhood. The 1927 Madam Walker theatre survives as its anchor.
insights.implication: Nowhere else do Indy's music and basketball histories share a street, so this is the market's strongest heritage story. Make it with the Madam Walker Legacy Center and the Crispus Attucks Museum, and credit and pay both. Never turn it into jazz-age nostalgia graphics.

insights.title: The real anthem is a 1917 song
insights.detail: "Back Home Again in Indiana" is sung before every Indy 500, and Jim Nabors sang it for four decades, through 2014. Louis Armstrong's All Stars often opened with it, and Charlie Parker's bebop standard "Donna Lee" is built on its chord changes. The 1917 composition is in the U.S. public domain.
insights.implication: With Haliburton back from his Achilles tear, "Back Home Again" is the obvious line for the home opener and the bounce-back season. The lyric and melody are free to use. Specific recordings (Nabors' included) and every Indy 500 mark are not.

insights.title: Indianapolis is the marching-arts capital
insights.detail: Drum Corps International, Music for All (Bands of America) and the Percussive Arts Society are all headquartered here. In August the DCI World Championships fill Lucas Oil Stadium, blocks from the Fieldhouse. The ISSMA state finals, BOA Grand Nationals and PASIC follow in November. Suburban programs like Carmel and Avon are perennial national powers, and pep bands still drive the small-town gym.
insights.implication: Drumline is the market's native sound of sport. Build band-jacket silhouettes, gauntlet cuffs and brass hardware into product. Hire Indiana high-school drumlines to play launches, and send the proceeds to band programs.

insights.title: The R&B line runs from Carr to Babyface
insights.detail: An Indianapolis duo cut Leroy Carr's 1928 "How Long, How Long Blues," and the Ink Spots formed here in the early 1930s. The line runs on to Kenneth "Babyface" Edmonds, a North Central High School alum whose brothers formed After 7. Babyface is the city's marquee living music name.
insights.implication: A premium "Naptown Soul" lifestyle story (satin, suede, monochrome navy) suits this lineage better than hype graphics. A Babyface collaboration would be the big get, on his team's terms.

insights.title: Two Indianas: the Avenue and the county seat
insights.detail: Pacers fandom is statewide. Rural Indiana's soundtrack is John Mellencamp's heartland rock (he's a Seymour native; think "Small Town" and "Pink Houses"). It's also Bill Monroe's Bean Blossom bluegrass festival in Brown County, held every June since 1967. Richmond's Gennett Records cut King Oliver's band with a young Louis Armstrong in 1923, and Hoagy Carmichael's "Stardust" in 1927.
insights.implication: Statewide product should cite named Indiana songs, towns and studios, not generic barns-and-cornfields Midwest imagery. Mellencamp's lyrics and likeness need licensing.

insights.title: The Pacers' own sound: "Boom Baby!"
insights.detail: Bobby "Slick" Leonard coached the ABA Pacers to titles in 1970, 1972 and 1973. He then called Pacers threes on the radio for decades with "Boom Baby!", the franchise's best-loved piece of audio. The Moments Mixtape City Edition (white, royal blue and gold) is reportedly returning for 2026-27, and its name already frames team history as a track list.
insights.implication: Nike co-owns the uniform's metaphor, so extend it. Use cassette J-card graphics, a "Side B" lifestyle drop and a mix commissioned from Indy DJs. Use "Boom Baby!" as the audio hook in launch content once the team and Leonard's estate clear it.

places.name: Madam Walker Legacy Center
places.why: Madam C.J. Walker's company built this 1927 terra-cotta theatre. It's the surviving anchor of the Avenue's jazz era and the essential partner for any Avenue story.

places.name: Crispus Attucks Museum
places.why: It tells the story of the 1955-56 Attucks champions, who shared a neighborhood with the Avenue's jazz clubs. That bridges the music and basketball lenses.

places.name: The Jazz Kitchen
places.why: Indy's flagship jazz room since 1994, where local and touring players keep the Montgomery-Hubbard lineage going.

places.name: Chatterbox Jazz Club
places.why: A tiny, decades-old late-night jazz bar. Plugged-in locals rate it above any downtown tourist stop.

places.name: Old National Centre (Murat Theatre and Egyptian Room)
places.why: The Murat Shrine complex is Indy's mid-size touring stage. The Egyptian Room is a rite-of-passage hip-hop and rock room.

places.name: The Vogue
places.why: A 1938 movie house, and Broad Ripple's anchor rock and dance club since the late 1970s.

places.name: HI-FI Indy
places.why: The small independent room at the center of Fountain Square's local and indie bills.

places.name: Luna Music
places.why: Indy's best-known independent record store, and the natural home for numbered, record-style product drops.

places.name: Lucas Oil Stadium
places.why: Hosts the DCI World Championships, BOA Grand Nationals and ISSMA state finals, a short walk from Gainbridge Fieldhouse.

places.name: Rhythm! Discovery Center
places.why: The Percussive Arts Society's hands-on drum museum, a ready-made partner for drumline product stories.

people.name: Wes Montgomery
people.why: Indy's most influential musician. He worked factory shifts by day and played Avenue clubs at night, and his thumb-picked octaves changed jazz guitar.

people.name: Freddie Hubbard
people.why: An Indianapolis native who came up with the Montgomery brothers before becoming a Blue Note star. He's part of the Avenue's export line.

people.name: David Baker
people.why: A Crispus Attucks alum and Avenue player who founded Indiana University's jazz studies program, linking the Avenue to Bloomington.

people.name: Leroy Carr
people.why: With guitarist Scrapper Blackwell he made "How Long, How Long Blues" (1928), which put Indianapolis on the early blues map.

people.name: Kenneth 'Babyface' Edmonds
people.why: The city's marquee living music name: born in Indianapolis, a North Central High School alum, with brothers who formed After 7.

people.name: John Mellencamp
people.why: A Seymour native based near Bloomington and a devoted Indiana hoops fan, he's the voice of the small-town Indiana that fills Pacers fandom.

people.name: Bobby 'Slick' Leonard
people.role: ABA-champion Pacers coach and longtime radio analyst (1932-2021)
people.why: His "Boom Baby!" three-point call is the franchise's signature sound.

people.name: Music for All
people.role: Indianapolis nonprofit that runs Bands of America
people.why: Its Grand National Championships at Lucas Oil each November are the marching-band world's Final Four. Its programs are a natural home for proceeds.

moments.name: IHSAA boys' basketball state finals
moments.why: Hoosier Hysteria peaks with small-town pep bands playing fight songs inside Gainbridge Fieldhouse. It's the clearest overlap of school music and basketball in the state.

moments.name: Indy 500 race weekend (Carb Day concert, Snake Pit, 'Back Home Again in Indiana')
moments.why: The state's biggest communal music moment: 300,000-plus people go silent for "Back Home Again" before the green flag.

moments.name: Bill Monroe's Bean Blossom Bluegrass Festival
moments.why: Running since 1967 in Brown County, it's a pilgrimage to rural Indiana's acoustic roots.

moments.name: Indy Jazz Fest
moments.why: The city's jazz showcase, and the logical summer stage for an Avenue-heritage preview.

moments.name: Indiana Black Expo Summer Celebration
moments.why: Black Indy's biggest annual gathering since 1971, with concerts. The right launch window for an Avenue capsule made with Black Indy creators.

moments.name: DCI World Championships
moments.why: The world's top drum corps take over Lucas Oil Stadium and downtown, a ready-made audience for a drumline-inspired preseason drop.

moments.name: Pacers home opener: Haliburton's return
moments.why: Haliburton's first Fieldhouse game back from his Achilles tear is the "Back Home Again" night.

moments.name: Marching November: ISSMA state finals, BOA Grand Nationals and PASIC
moments.why: Indiana's band families and the global percussion world converge downtown in the season's first weeks. Perfect for a Fieldhouse drumline night.

vocabulary.meaning: A jazz-era nickname for Indianapolis, worn with pride in Black Indy and local hip-hop. It's affectionate from insiders, so let local creators lead.
Indiana Avenue, the historic Black business and jazz district northwest of downtown.
Slick Leonard's radio call for a Pacers three, still shouted by fans and used by the team.
Shorthand for "Back Home Again in Indiana," the song sung before the Indy 500 and the state's emotional anthem.
What locals still call Ruoff Music Center, the Noblesville amphitheater, decades after the name changed.
The Friday before the Indy 500: final practice, pit-stop competition and a big infield concert.
The EDM festival inside Turn 3 of the Speedway on race day, and Indiana's biggest dance-music crowd.
"South of Broad Ripple," the College Ave strip that's home to the Jazz Kitchen and Luna Music.

designCues.cue: Walker terra cotta: the warm fired-clay color of the Avenue's 1927 theatre
designCues.source: The terra-cotta facade and Africanesque Art Deco ornament of the Madam Walker Legacy Center on Indiana Avenue.
designCues.use: Use it as a base or accent beside Pacers navy for an Avenue capsule made with the Center. Take the color only. The ornament and African-derived motifs are off limits unless the Center partners and is credited. The hex is approximate, so lab-match it.

designCues.cue: Sousaphone brass: a darker, metallic counterpart to Pacers gold
designCues.source: The brass lines of Indiana marching bands and the drum corps that fill Lucas Oil every August.
designCues.use: Use it for metal hardware, foil prints, aglets and zipper pulls beside Pacers gold (#FDBB30) for a brass-and-gold tone-on-tone. It's approximate, so match it with a metallic lab dip.

designCues.cue: Octaves: two parallel lines a fixed interval apart
designCues.source: Wes Montgomery's thumb-picked octave technique, the signature sound of Indianapolis jazz.
designCues.use: Run it as a double pinstripe, sleeve taping or side-panel piping. It's an abstract nod that needs no likeness, but naming Wes on product requires his estate's license.

designCues.cue: Drum-corps band jacket: high collar, asymmetric sash panel, gauntlet cuffs
designCues.source: DCI and Bands of America uniforms, centered on Lucas Oil Stadium each August and November.
designCues.use: Turn it into a warmup jacket or shooting shirt with a diagonal sash panel and oversized ribbed gauntlet cuffs. Never copy a specific corps' or school's uniform.

designCues.cue: 1917 sheet-music script for "Back Home Again in Indiana"
designCues.source: The original public-domain sheet music of the Indy 500's pre-race song.
designCues.use: Redraw the lettering for a "Back Home Again" chest or neck lockup on home-opener product. Keep it apart from Indy 500 marks, checkered flags and the wing-and-wheel.

designCues.cue: Cassette J-card track list of Pacers moments
designCues.source: The Moments Mixtape City Edition, plus moments fans would put on it. Those are the ABA titles ('70, '72, '73), Reggie's 8 points in 8.9 seconds at MSG (1995) and Haliburton's 2025 Finals Game 1 winner.
designCues.use: Print it on hangtags, inside necks and jacket linings as a "Side A / Side B" track list. Check the official uniform design first, so the extension matches it without duplicating it.

designCues.cue: 78-rpm groove texture: "Richmond, Ind., 1923"
designCues.source: Gennett Records in Richmond, where King Oliver's band with Louis Armstrong and Hoagy Carmichael ("Stardust") first recorded.
designCues.use: Use a fine concentric groove emboss on patches or hangtags for a statewide heritage story. Tell it only with Gennett's full history in mind (see watchouts).

productHooks: A "Back Home Again" home-opener capsule for late October 2026. It's a shooting shirt and tee in the returning Moments Mixtape white, royal and gold, with the public-domain 1917 lyric in sheet-music script. Frame it as the team's return, not as Haliburton signature product.
A Moments Mixtape "Side B" lifestyle drop: cassette J-card hangtags, an inside-neck track list and a launch mix commissioned from Indy DJs and producers. Sell it as a numbered run at Luna Music.

A drumline warmup pack with a band-jacket warmup, gauntlet cuffs and sousaphone-brass hardware. Debut it in the November marching weeks, with an Indiana high-school drumline playing a Fieldhouse game and proceeds going to Music for All band programs.

An Avenue capsule co-designed with the Madam Walker Legacy Center and Black Indy artists, in Walker terra cotta, navy and octave stripes. Launch it at Indiana Black Expo Summer Celebration in July, with a revenue share to the Center.
A "Boom Baby!" three-point tee with a sound-on QR to Slick Leonard's archival call. Release it after a Pacers three-point milestone night, subject to clearance from the team and Leonard's estate.
watchouts: Brand conflict: Haliburton signed with Puma in Oct 2024 (signature-line naming unconfirmed). Keep anything celebrating his return team-level, use only NBA-licensed player assets, and keep "Hali" naming off Nike product.

Indiana Avenue is Black heritage shaped by displacement. Urban renewal, I-65 and the IUPUI campus cleared much of the near-westside. Co-create with the Madam Walker Legacy Center, the Crispus Attucks Museum and Black Indy artists, and pay them. Don't borrow jazz-age imagery.

IP and clearance: The Speedway owns the Indy 500, Carb Day, Snake Pit, checkered-flag and wing-and-wheel marks. Recordings of "Back Home Again" (Nabors' included) are copyrighted even though the 1917 song is not. Corps and school uniforms belong to their organizations. The names, likenesses and lyrics of Wes Montgomery, Babyface and Mellencamp all need licensing.

Gennett Records also pressed private Ku Klux Klan records in the 1920s, when the Klan dominated Indiana politics. Use its jazz story only with that history in mind, and never as unexamined "Indiana heritage" nostalgia.

Swap risk and currency: cornfields-and-barns heartland imagery is generic and can caricature rural Indiana. Anchor small-town cues in named Indiana songs and pep bands. Reconfirm venue names, festival dates and the current hip-hop scene before acting, because this dossier is from model knowledge.

art.headline: Indianapolis looks like limestone, fieldhouse brick and blue-and-gold civic heraldry.
art.summary: Indianapolis looks planned and civic: Ralston's circle-and-diagonals grid, limestone monuments and a state flag whose gold torch on blue already matches the Pacers' navy and gold. The game's own look comes from the gym, in felt banners, block letters and painted maple. LOVE and the Speedway's marks are licensed IP, so the opening is living local artists, starting with Black artists on Indiana Avenue.

insights.title: Art districts ride Ralston's diagonals
insights.detail: Alexander Ralston's 1821 Mile Square sent four diagonal avenues out from the center. Three now carry the city's art districts. Massachusetts Ave has Pamela Bliss's 2011 Vonnegut mural and Julian Opie's "Ann Dancing." Virginia Ave runs out to Fountain Square, home to the Murphy Art Center and the 1928 Fountain Square Theatre's neon. Indiana Ave has the Madam Walker Legacy Center.
insights.implication: Organize a city capsule around the circle-and-diagonals map. Give each avenue its own artist and drop, so together they read as one Indianapolis system, not a skyline.

insights.title: The fieldhouse is Indiana's native architecture
insights.detail: Hinkle Fieldhouse (1928) hosted the state finals through 1971, including Milan's 1954 title and the "Hoosiers" finale. New Castle's gym seats roughly 7,300 (once about 9,300) and is billed as the world's largest high-school gym. Gainbridge Fieldhouse (1999) is a brick-and-steel-truss homage to that lineage, and locals just call it "the Fieldhouse."
insights.implication: Design from the gym out: felt banners, chenille block letters, painted maple and truss geometry. Every motorsport town already uses racing checkers.

insights.title: The team palette is the state flag
insights.detail: Paul Hadley's 1916 Indiana flag sets a gold torch and 19 stars on blue. That makes Pacers navy #002D62 and gold #FDBB30 civic colors, not just team colors. The white, royal and gold Moments Mixtape City Edition returns for 2026-27.
insights.implication: Lifestyle product can borrow the flag's geometry (the 13-5-1 star arrangement, the torch rays) to feel Hoosier without a logo. That complements the returning City Edition instead of repeating it.

insights.title: Indiana Avenue is the deepest untapped source
insights.detail: The 1927 Madam Walker building, by Rubush & Hunter, wears Africanesque terra cotta over the Avenue of Wes Montgomery's and Freddie Hubbard's jazz. Crispus Attucks, whose Oscar Robertson-led team won the 1955 state title, is nearby. In 2020, 18 Black artists painted "BLACK LIVES MATTER" down the street. The postwar IU/IUPUI campus expansion that displaced the neighborhood is still living memory.
insights.implication: Build the Celebration of Black History product with the Madam Walker Legacy Center, the Crispus Attucks Museum and paid Black Indianapolis artists, and give revenue back to them. Generic Black History graphics would waste this source.

insights.title: Indiana's pop-art icon painted Milwaukee's court
insights.detail: New Castle-born Robert Indiana took his surname from the state, and Newfields holds his original LOVE sculpture. But the NBA floor he painted was the Bucks' 1977 MECCA court.
insights.implication: His estate controls the state's most famous graphic language, and a division rival already owns its court story. Commission living Indiana artists for court and graphic work instead of LOVE homages.

insights.title: Indy upcycles its arenas
insights.detail: When the RCA Dome came down in 2008, People for Urban Progress turned its roof fabric into bags, wallets and shade structures. It's a known local model for giving a sports building a second life as civic product.
insights.implication: Make an upcycled line with PUP from retired Pacers banners, court boards or Fieldhouse signage. It gives Nike's sustainability work a hometown story.

insights.title: Murals follow mega-events, then fade
insights.detail: The Arts Council's 46 for XLVI put 46 murals on city walls for the 2012 Super Bowl. A number have since faded or been lost to redevelopment. The city leans on hosting (the Super Bowl, the 2024 NBA All-Star Game) to fund public art.
insights.implication: Be the steady patron instead of another one-off event layer. Keep a roster of Indy muralists working through Haliburton's comeback season.

places.name: Madam Walker Legacy Center
places.why: The 1927 Africanesque landmark and its Casino ballroom anchor the Avenue's Black arts and jazz history. It's the essential partner for any Indiana Avenue work.

places.name: Newfields (Indianapolis Museum of Art)
places.why: Holds Robert Indiana's original LOVE sculpture and the 100 Acres art park. It also stewards Saarinen and Girard's Miller House in Columbus, the state's modernist design canon.

places.name: Herron School of Art + Design
places.why: The state's flagship art school, and the pipeline for local illustrators, printmakers and visual-communication designers.

places.name: Harrison Center
places.why: A former church full of studios. It anchors First Friday and the city's artist-as-neighbor programs.

places.name: Murphy Art Center
places.why: A converted dime-store building at the heart of Fountain Square's First Friday, a short walk from the neon of the 1928 Fountain Square Theatre.

places.name: Tube Factory artspace (Big Car Collaborative)
places.why: Big Car's converted factory is the Southside's center for socially engaged art and neighborhood-made public projects.

places.name: Indianapolis Art Center
places.why: Michael Graves designed the building, and it hosts the Broad Ripple Art Fair every May.

places.name: Eiteljorg Museum
places.why: Native American and Western art, the Indian Market each June and a Contemporary Art Fellowship. Call it first on any Indigenous design question.

places.name: Hinkle Fieldhouse
places.why: The 1928 gym of Milan '54 and "Hoosiers," and the visual template for the brick, truss and daylight look of Indiana basketball.

places.name: Massachusetts Avenue
places.why: Ralston's northeast diagonal. It's home to Pamela Bliss's Vonnegut mural, Opie's LED "Ann Dancing" on the Cultural Trail, and galleries.

people.name: Robert Indiana (estate)
people.role: Pop artist (1928-2018), born in New Castle
people.why: Made LOVE and painted the Bucks' MECCA floor. He's the state's most famous graphic voice, and his estate tightly controls the imagery.

people.name: Big Car Collaborative
people.role: Artist collective founded by Jim Walker; runs Tube Factory and community radio
people.why: A credible, neighborhood-rooted partner for commissioning and paying local artists on a Pacers project.

people.name: Pamela Bliss
people.why: Her 2011 Kurt Vonnegut portrait on Mass Ave is the city's best-known mural, which makes her a proven hand for large portrait walls.

people.name: People for Urban Progress
people.role: Upcycling and design nonprofit founded by Michael Bricker
people.why: Turned the RCA Dome roof into products and public shade structures. A ready partner for upcycled Pacers material.

people.name: Arts Council of Indianapolis
people.role: City arts agency and public-art commissioner
people.why: Ran 46 for XLVI and keeps the roster of local muralists, so it can route a mural program to vetted artists.

people.name: Michael Graves
people.role: Indianapolis-born postmodern architect and product designer (1934-2015)
people.why: Designed the Indianapolis Art Center, and proved an Indy designer could take playful civic forms to mass-market product.

people.name: Florence Griffith Joyner
people.why: Credited with designing the Pacers' 1990-97 uniforms, the Reggie Miller-era look fans know best.

people.name: Penske Entertainment (Indianapolis Motor Speedway)
people.role: Owner of IMS and the Indianapolis 500
people.why: Owns the wing-and-wheel, "Brickyard" and Indy 500 marks. A racing crossover needs its license.

moments.name: First Friday gallery night
moments.why: Harrison Center, Murphy Art Center and other studios open together. It's the natural drop night for artist-series product.

moments.name: IHSAA boys basketball state finals
moments.why: Small-town gym colors, letter jackets and banners from across the state converge on the Fieldhouse.

moments.name: Broad Ripple Art Fair
moments.why: The Indianapolis Art Center's long-running fair opens the outdoor art season and lands during the playoffs.

moments.name: Indianapolis 500 / Month of May
moments.why: The city's biggest graphics takeover, with checkered flags and bricks everywhere, overlaps a potential Pacers playoff run.

moments.name: Talbot Street Art Fair
moments.why: A long-running juried fair in the Herron-Morton Place historic district, and the scene's summer gathering.

moments.name: Eiteljorg Indian Market and Festival
moments.why: Native artists from across the country sell directly. This is the place to meet Indigenous artists properly.

moments.name: Penrod Arts Fair
moments.why: Hundreds of artists on the Newfields grounds, and the last big art crowd before tip-off.

moments.name: Circle of Lights
moments.why: The Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument has been lit as a giant tree since 1962, a ready-made holiday graphic for the early season.

vocabulary.meaning: Indianapolis, after Monument Circle at the center of the Mile Square.
An old, once-derisive nickname that locals, rappers and makers have reclaimed with affection. Use it lightly.
The original 1821 downtown plat, bounded by East, West, North and South streets.
Indiana Avenue, the historic center of Black business, jazz and culture.
What locals call the Pacers' arena, whatever the sponsor name is.
The state's basketball fever, especially the single-class tournament era that ended in 1997.
The state motto since 1937, for the roads and rails that meet here.
The Indianapolis Motor Speedway, paved with 3.2 million bricks in 1909. A yard of them still marks the finish line.

designCues.cue: Torch gold #FDBB30 on Fieldhouse navy #002D62, read as the state flag rather than just team colors
designCues.source: Paul Hadley's 1916 Indiana flag: a gold torch and stars on a blue field
designCues.use: Lead lifestyle product with gold on navy and frame the pairing as Hoosier heraldry. Keep royal for the returning City Edition.

designCues.cue: Statehouse limestone buff, a warm off-white with fine oolitic grain
designCues.source: Bedford-Bloomington limestone in the Statehouse, the Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument and the Scottish Rite Cathedral
designCues.use: Use it as the neutral base in place of stark white on fleece and caps, with a honed-stone texture print on trims.

designCues.cue: Ring of 13 stars, inner arc of 5 and a single star above a rayed torch
designCues.source: The Indiana state flag, where the top star marks Indiana as the 19th state
designCues.use: Use it as a neck tape, jock tag or tonal emboss. The 19 stars carry the story without a logo.

designCues.cue: Circle and four diagonals: a center disc with spokes running out to a square
designCues.source: Ralston's 1821 Mile Square plan and Roger Gohl's 1963 city flag (a white star on a red disc ringed in white)
designCues.use: Use it as a crest, an all-over map pattern or a court-center graphic that links the Mass Ave, Fountain Square and Indiana Ave drops.

designCues.cue: Felt-banner and chenille block lettering: tall slab capitals with outline strokes, hand-painted center-court logos
designCues.source: Indiana high-school gyms from Hinkle (1928) to New Castle, with town banners hung from the rafters
designCues.use: Put chenille and tackle-twill letters on varsity jackets and warmups, in custom letterforms drawn by Indiana designers.

designCues.cue: Single strip of worn red brick, laid like the finish line
designCues.source: The Yard of Bricks at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, and the Pacers name itself, which comes from the 500 pace car and harness-racing pacers
designCues.use: Run an unbranded brick strip across a hem or waistband as a "pace line." Any IMS mark or trophy imagery needs a license.

designCues.cue: Neon-tube monoline script on vertical blade signs
designCues.source: The marquees of the Fountain Square Theatre (1928) and Broad Ripple's Vogue (1938)
designCues.use: Use it for night-game and holiday wordmarks. Draw new letterforms in this tradition instead of copying either sign.

designCues.cue: Africanesque terra-cotta geometry: stepped borders, stylized figures and chevrons
designCues.source: The 1927 Madam Walker building on Indiana Avenue
designCues.use: Use only in a co-design with the Madam Walker Legacy Center and paid Black Indianapolis artists. Credit them on product and return revenue.

productHooks: "Fieldhouse Felt" varsity jacket and warmup: chenille block INDIANA, felt-banner graphics, painted-maple lining and a 19-star neck tape. Launch at Hinkle and the Fieldhouse around the late-March state finals.

"Four Diagonals" First Friday series: four limited tees and hoodies for Mass Ave, Fountain Square, Indiana Ave and Monument Circle. Each is by a paid local artist from Herron, Harrison Center or Big Car.
Celebration of Black History capsule, co-designed with the Madam Walker Legacy Center and the Crispus Attucks Museum. It honors Oscar Robertson's 1955 Tigers, with a revenue share to both.
"Pace" May playoff pack: limestone tees with a brick pace stripe, dropped in Indy 500 week. Any IMS mark is licensed through Penske Entertainment.
Upcycled bags and accessories cut from retired Pacers banners, court boards and Fieldhouse signage, made with People for Urban Progress.
"Circle of Lights" holiday tee and ornament: the monument drawn as a tree in limestone and gold neon script, released the Friday after Thanksgiving.
watchouts: Robert Indiana's LOVE, his numbers and his stenciled-word works are controlled by his estate and licensees, after years of litigation involving the Morgan Art Foundation. Don't use stacked lettering with a tilted O, or other homages, without a license.
Licensed IP: the IMS wing-and-wheel, "Indianapolis 500," "The Brickyard" and the Borg-Warner Trophy belong to IMS/Penske Entertainment. "Hoosiers" and the Hickory Huskers are film IP.

Indiana Avenue's displacement by campus expansion and the interstate is living memory. Never use the Walker building's motifs or the Avenue's history as decoration. Co-design with Black Indianapolis artists and institutions, and pay and credit them.

Newfields' 2021 job posting about keeping its "traditional, core, white art audience" forced the CEO out and left distrust among Black artists. A Newfields partnership alone doesn't signal community buy-in.

Indiana was Myaamia, Lenape, Potawatomi and Shawnee land, so any Native reference goes only through the Eiteljorg and tribal artists. Likewise, the Southside Burmese Chin community's textiles are for Chin-led partners only.

food.headline: Indiana eats like a Friday-night gym: tenderloins wider than the bun, sugar cream pie.
food.summary: Indiana's food is proud, plain and oversized, from the breaded pork tenderloin that hangs off its bun to sugar cream pie and gym-concession popcorn. Game nights run through century-old downtown institutions a short walk from Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Newer Indy cooks in Fletcher Place and two immigrant corridors. This is written from model knowledge, so scout the arena vendors and newer spots before anyone acts.

insights.title: The tenderloin is judged by its overhang
insights.detail: Indiana's signature sandwich is a pork loin pounded thin, breaded, fried and served far wider than its bun. Nick's Kitchen in Huntington claims the 1908 original. In Indy the classic carriers are drive-ins and taverns like Mug-n-Bun in Speedway (1960, carhops and house root beer) and Plump's Last Shot in Broad Ripple. The Indiana Foodways Alliance maps a statewide tenderloin trail.
insights.implication: "Bigger than the bun" is a graphic idea locals already love: a shape that breaks its own frame. Run it as a playful overhang motif on caps and tees. Make it a paid, licensed collab with a named drive-in, not generic food clip art.

insights.title: St. Elmo's shrimp cocktail is downtown's power ritual
insights.detail: St. Elmo Steak House has served steaks a few blocks from the Fieldhouse since 1902. Its shrimp cocktail comes buried in a horseradish-heavy sauce that clears the sinuses. Every first-timer gets dared to eat it, and the sauce sells in jars in Indiana grocery stores. The Huse family's restaurant is the big-night table for Pacers, Colts and Indy 500 crowds.
insights.implication: Cocktail red and horseradish cream make an insider colorway story any Hoosier will recognize. Using the St. Elmo name, its 1902 mark or the jar label needs a license and a paid partnership.

insights.title: Hoosier Hysteria has a concession stand
insights.detail: Statewide basketball religion is lived in small-town gyms like New Castle Fieldhouse (the largest high school gym in the world) and the Hoosier Gym in Knightstown. There, the popcorn machine and a menu board of tenderloins and pie are part of the ritual. Indiana is one of the nation's top popcorn producers, and Orville Redenbacher was a Hoosier. In Broad Ripple, Bobby Plump, whose shot won Milan's 1954 state title, lent his name to Plump's Last Shot, a restaurant full of that history.
insights.implication: A gym-concessions capsule (popcorn stripes, menu-board type, a "Last Shot" story) ties the Pacers to the statewide high school game, not just downtown. Time it to the IHSAA state finals, played at Gainbridge in March.

insights.title: Sugar cream pie is a humble state treasure
insights.detail: Sugar cream pie, Indiana's official state pie since 2009, came out of east-central Indiana's Shaker and Amish kitchens. It's a "desperation pie," made from pantry staples when the fruit ran out: cream, sugar and a dusting of nutmeg. Wick's Pies in Winchester has made it at scale since the 1940s.
insights.implication: A custard-cream base with a nutmeg-speckle texture makes a warm winter colorway. It sits naturally beside the white, royal blue and gold of the returning Moments Mixtape City Edition. Nobody owns the pie, so the palette is free to use. Wick's branding is not.

insights.title: The new food city: Lafayette Road and the Southside
insights.detail: The International Marketplace on the northwest side packs Mexican, West African, Vietnamese, Middle Eastern and South Asian restaurants and grocers along Lafayette Road. The Southside (Perry Township toward Southport and Greenwood) is home to the largest Chin refugee community in the U.S. Its restaurants serve dishes like sabuti, a hominy-corn soup.
insights.implication: These neighborhoods hold many of Indy's newer fans and rarely show up in Pacers product. Commission anything here through the International Marketplace Coalition and Chin community organizations, and credit and pay local artists. Never mash the cultures into a generic "world food" graphic.

insights.title: Fletcher Place chefs and a feeding mission
insights.detail: Jonathan Brooks's Milktooth (he was a Food & Wine Best New Chef in 2016) and Bluebeard, named for the Kurt Vonnegut novel, made Fletcher Place the city's chef-driven strip. Milktooth briefly closed in early 2026 for an Arlene's conversion and is reportedly returning. Martha Hoover's Patachou group runs Public Greens, whose profits help fund the Patachou Foundation's meals for food-insecure kids.
insights.implication: Hoover's foundation is a credible community-investment partner for a Cup-week or holiday giving night. Fletcher Place is a design-forward setting for a launch dinner. Confirm both restaurants are still operating first.

insights.title: 2026-27 gives the food map a basketball calendar
insights.detail: Haliburton returns in a season when Indiana hosts the 76ers and new Sixer LeBron James on the Oct 30 Cup Night. The Dec 11 NBA Cup final comes to Butler's Hinkle Fieldhouse. Fans will fill the Fieldhouse corridor (St. Elmo, the Slippery Noodle, Bicentennial Unity Plaza) and the old College Avenue taverns near Hinkle, like the Red Key.
insights.implication: Build a "Gainbridge to Hinkle" Cup-week food-map capsule that works whether or not the Pacers reach the final. Keep it team- and city-led, because Haliburton's signature footwear sits with another brand, not Nike.

places.name: St. Elmo Steak House

places.name: Slippery Noodle Inn
places.neighborhood: Downtown (South Meridian St, near Union Station)
places.why: Indiana's oldest bar (1850) has live blues and sits just south of the Fieldhouse, a walkable stop before or after the game.

places.why: The Fieldhouse's outdoor plaza hosts Pacers watch parties and winter skating. It's the natural home for food-truck and product pop-ups.

places.name: Shapiro's Delicatessen
places.why: A cafeteria-line Jewish deli since 1905. Corned beef and cheesecake before a game is a long-running Indy habit.

places.name: Long's Bakery
places.why: Cash-only glazed yeast doughnuts since 1955. The line out the door and the plain white box are pure Indy.

places.name: Mug-n-Bun

places.name: Plump's Last Shot

people.role: Milan High's 1954 state-title hero and namesake of Plump's Last Shot

people.role: Owner of Huse Culinary (St. Elmo Steak House, Harry & Izzy's)

people.why: The best-known commercial sugar cream pie in the state, and licensable for a Hoosier-pie hangtag or launch giveaway.

moments.why: St. Elmo, the Slippery Noodle and Shapiro's, all within walking distance, are where Pacers nights start.

moments.why: A national basketball audience comes to Butler-Tarkington, so the College Avenue taverns and downtown restaurants become the Cup-week food map.

moments.why: Indy's Chin community celebrates its national day with food and traditional dress. Engage only by invitation and partnership.

moments.why: Pork-tent tenderloins, Dairy Barn milkshakes and elephant ears make it the state's biggest food gathering, right in the NBA offseason.

culture.headline: Indiana knows it's basketball's capital, even if the coasts only see flyover country
culture.summary: Local pride runs on Hoosier Hysteria, Milan's 1954 upset at Hinkle and Oscar Robertson's Crispus Attucks titles, plus the Pacers' ABA dynasty and Reggie Miller's feud with New York. The team carries the state's name, so the market reaches every county gym. Build a heritage season from gyms, brackets and Black Indianapolis history, peaking at Hinkle on Dec 11 and the Knicks games.

insights.title: Home of the game, treated as flyover
insights.detail: Hoosiers quote Naismith's 1925 verdict that basketball 'really had its origin in Indiana, which remains the center of the sport.' They resent being treated as a small-market afterthought. The 2025 Finals ratings talk sharpened that feeling. Moving the NBA Cup final from Las Vegas to Hinkle Fieldhouse reads locally as overdue recognition.
insights.implication: Speak with authority, as in 'where the game lives'. Skip underdog self-pity like 'small market, big heart'. Make Dec 11 the season's top heritage window, whether or not the Pacers reach the final. Complement the white, royal and gold 'Moments Mixtape' City Edition instead of competing with it.

insights.title: Two founding myths: Milan '54 and Attucks '55
insights.detail: Tiny Milan beat Muncie Central at Hinkle in 1954, the game that became 'Hoosiers'. A year later Crispus Attucks, the city's segregated Black high school, won the state title with Oscar Robertson. It was the first all-Black school in the nation to win an open state championship. The city let the team circle Monument Circle once, then sent its celebration to Northwestern Park.
insights.implication: Milan is well-worn. Attucks is the more Indianapolis story, and the less told. Build it with the Crispus Attucks Museum and its alumni for a February release. Put both stories in one heritage system so neither erases the other.

insights.title: Indiana's team, not Indianapolis's
insights.detail: Like the Fever, the Pacers carry the state's name. Fans run from 317 out to the 765 and 812 towns, where gyms can seat more people than live there. New Castle Fieldhouse seats roughly 7,300 after renovation (once about 9,300). At the edges, the Region (219) leans toward Chicago and southern Indiana toward Louisville and Kentucky. IU against Purdue divides everyone in between.
insights.implication: Make statewide product (area codes, county numbers, town gyms) and sell it outside Marion County. Don't push Pacers loyalty into Bulls or Kentucky territory, and never take a side in IU against Purdue.

insights.title: New York is the civic rival
insights.detail: Reggie Miller's choke sign at Spike Lee in 1994 and his 8 points in 8.9 seconds at MSG on May 7, 1995 cast it as a small Midwestern city against the media capital. Haliburton revived the rivalry with his own choke gesture after his Game 1 shot in the 2025 East finals, which Indiana won 4-2. The Knicks are now defending champions and share the Pacers' NBA Cup group.
insights.implication: Knicks dates are the season's best rivalry drops. Lean on numerals and dates ('8.9', '5.7.95') instead of mocking Knicks fans. License Reggie's name or likeness wherever it appears.

insights.title: Racing is in the name
insights.detail: The Pacers took their name in 1967 from the Indy 500 pace car and harness-racing pacers. May is the city's civic high season: the Mini-Marathon, Carb Day, the 500 Festival Parade and the race itself. 'Back Home Again in Indiana' is sung before the start, and milk is drunk in victory lane.
insights.implication: Speed, pace lines, checkered rhythm and race-number roundels are earned motifs here, and they suit a team that wins by pushing tempo. Keep IMS marks out unless licensed. Time a May capsule to the 2027 second round.

insights.title: People rep their side of town
insights.detail: Locals identify by side of town. The Eastside has Irvington and its Halloween Festival. The Westside has Haughville and the town of Speedway. The Northside has Broad Ripple, the canal-and-Monon bar village. The Southside has Fountain Square's arts scene, Greenwood and the Chin (Burmese) community around Southport. Mass Ave is the walkable strip nearest the Fieldhouse. Hamilton County (Carmel with its roundabouts, Fishers) holds much of the suburban fan base.
insights.implication: A four-sides series, co-made with local designers and sold through each neighborhood, will travel further than another generic 'Indy' tee.

insights.title: Gray winters are lived in gyms
insights.detail: Basketball fills Indiana's cold, overcast half-year from November to March. Friday nights mean overheated gyms, letter jackets, layered hoodies and seed caps. Summer is hot and humid, built around the State Fair, the 500's infield and pickup games on driveway hoops.
insights.implication: Release heavyweight fleece, varsity jackets, beanies and quarter-zips from November to March, peaking in sectional and state-finals weeks. Lightweight racing and fair product fits May through August.

places.name: Hinkle Fieldhouse
places.why: Butler's 1928 gym hosted the state finals through 1971, Milan's 1954 winner and the climax of 'Hoosiers'. On Dec 11, 2026 it hosts the NBA Cup championship.

places.name: Crispus Attucks High School and Crispus Attucks Museum
places.why: Home of Oscar Robertson's 1955 and 1956 state champions. The museum holds the history of segregated Indianapolis and the school's teams.

places.name: Indiana Avenue (Madam Walker Legacy Center)
places.why: Black Indianapolis's 'Avenue' of jazz clubs (Wes Montgomery, Freddie Hubbard, J.J. Johnson) and Madam C.J. Walker's company. University and highway expansion cleared much of it, and the Walker building anchors it today.

places.name: Monument Circle
places.why: The Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument gave the 'Circle City' its name. The city gathers here to celebrate, from the Circle of Lights to big wins.

places.name: Indiana Farmers Coliseum
places.why: The Pacers' first home. Slick Leonard's teams won ABA titles here in 1970, 1972 and 1973, before the 1974 move to Market Square Arena.

places.name: Indianapolis Motor Speedway
places.why: The source of the Pacers' name and of May's civic calendar.

places.name: Indiana Basketball Hall of Fame
places.why: The shrine to Hoosier Hysteria, next door to New Castle Fieldhouse, the largest high school gym in the world. It sits about an hour east of downtown.

places.name: Fountain Square
places.why: A working-class neighborhood turned arts and nightlife district, built around the 1928 Fountain Square Theatre Building. It sits at the southern end of the Cultural Trail.

places.name: Broad Ripple Village
places.why: A canal-side village on the Monon Trail with the city's longest-running bar strip. It is the Northside's identity in one place.

places.name: Massachusetts Avenue and the Bottleworks District
places.why: The diagonal theater and restaurant strip a few blocks from the Fieldhouse, on the Indy Pride parade route. It ends at Bottleworks, an Art Deco Coca-Cola plant turned hotel and food hall.

people.name: Oscar Robertson
people.role: Hall of Famer, Crispus Attucks 1955-56 state champion
people.why: Indianapolis's greatest homegrown player and the face of the Attucks story. Invite him into heritage work, don't just borrow his image.

people.name: Reggie Miller
people.why: Built the Knicks rivalry and remains Indiana's defining NBA star.

people.name: Larry Bird
people.role: Hall of Famer from French Lick; former Pacers coach and president
people.why: The small-town Hoosier ideal, from Indiana State to coaching the Pacers to the 2000 Finals.

people.name: Bobby 'Slick' Leonard (estate)
people.role: Coach of the three ABA titles, longtime Pacers radio voice
people.why: His 'Boom Baby!' call on Pacers threes is the market's best-loved catchphrase. He died in 2021.

people.name: Tamika Catchings
people.role: Indiana Fever legend, 2012 WNBA champion, Hall of Famer
people.why: Proof that Indianapolis took women's basketball seriously long before the Caitlin Clark boom. Her Catch the Stars Foundation, an Indianapolis youth nonprofit, is a credible youth-hoops partner that doesn't lean on a current star (confirm its current programs).

people.name: Caitlin Clark
people.why: Made the Fieldhouse the center of women's basketball and brought a younger, new fan base into the building the Pacers share.

people.name: Indiana Black Expo
people.why: Runs the July Summer Celebration and the Circle City Classic. The natural partner for Black Indianapolis heritage work.

people.name: Indiana High School Athletic Association (IHSAA)
people.why: Owns the state tournament and its marks, so it controls any sectional or state-finals product.

moments.name: Emirates NBA Cup championship at Hinkle Fieldhouse
moments.why: The first Cup final played outside Las Vegas, in the gym where Hoosier Hysteria grew up.

moments.name: Circle of Lights
moments.why: The Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument has been lit as a giant holiday tree since 1962. This year the lighting lands on an NBA Cup group-play Friday.

moments.name: IHSAA basketball state finals
moments.timing: Girls in early February; boys in late March, usually at Gainbridge Fieldhouse
moments.why: The living ritual of Hoosier Hysteria. Town buses and school colors fill downtown.

moments.name: Month of May and the Indianapolis 500
moments.timing: All of May; the race is on Memorial Day weekend Sunday (expected May 30, 2027)
moments.why: The city's biggest civic month, from the Mini-Marathon to the 500 Festival Parade. It overlaps the second round of the playoffs.

moments.name: Indy Pride
moments.why: A parade on Mass Ave and a festival downtown, blocks from the Fieldhouse. It's the high point of the year for LGBTQ+ Indianapolis.

moments.name: Indiana Black Expo Summer Celebration
moments.why: Running since the early 1970s, it is one of the Midwest's largest Black cultural gatherings, with basketball, music and business on the program.

moments.name: Indiana State Fair
moments.why: The statewide gathering, held on the grounds where the Pacers won their ABA titles.

moments.name: Circle City Classic
moments.why: Indiana Black Expo's HBCU football weekend and downtown parade, held since 1984, falls in the same weeks as Pacers tip-off.

vocabulary.meaning: Long-running nickname for Indianapolis, once a dig at a sleepy town and now worn with pride, especially in Black Indianapolis and local hip-hop. A Hudnut-era sports strategy turned Naptown into a host of Final Fours, a Super Bowl and the 2024 All-Star Game.
Civic nickname from Monument Circle, used by institutions (the Circle City Classic) and in local branding.
Statewide basketball fever, born from the single-class high school tournament. 'Hoosier' is the state demonym, of disputed origin, and belongs to everyone in Indiana, not just IU.
Indy's area code, worn as identity (463 is the overlay). 765, 812, 219, 574 and 260 mark the rest of the state.
What locals call the Pacers' arena through every sponsor (Conseco, Bankers Life, Gainbridge). Built in 1999, it was designed to feel like an Indiana gym.
Slick Leonard's radio call on a made three, still shouted and printed.
From 'Back Home Again in Indiana' (1917), sung before every Indy 500. Shorthand for coming home to Indiana.
Northwest Indiana (219), Chicago-facing and often Bulls country. Its natives call themselves Region rats.

designCues.use: Warm base for heritage fleece, wordmark fills and court-line prints. Pair it with Pacers navy #002D62 and gold #FDBB30, not Butler blue.

designCues.use: Use it as a back-yoke panel, sleeve graphic or tunnel-walk tee outline for Dec 11. Draw it generically unless Butler licenses the Hinkle name.

designCues.use: Use it as an all-over print or back graphic that can be customized with town names. Use IHSAA marks only under license.

underground.headline: Indy's underground runs on methanol, gym wax and dice
underground.summary: Indianapolis named its team after a pace car, and its deepest subculture is still motor oil: dirt-track bullrings, sprint cars and drag strips. The second is Hoosier Hysteria's pilgrims, who tour giant high school gyms and hoard sectional tees. Gen Con takes over downtown every summer. Punk, drag and DIY rooms are real but anti-corporate, and the sneaker conversation is split between Puma and Nike.

insights.title: Named for a pace car, raised in the bullrings
insights.detail: USAC, which sanctions sprint and midget racing, is headquartered in Speedway. Every July, Indiana Sprint Week runs a string of bullrings from Kokomo to Bloomington's red clay. Anderson's Little 500 (33 cars, 500 laps on a quarter-mile) runs the night before the Indy 500. Fans wear sun-faded crew shirts, Hoosier Racing Tire tees and hand-lettered car numbers. Kyle Larson's 2024 Indy 500-Coca-Cola 600 'Double' attempt pulled dirt-track fandom into IMS just as racing jackets went mainstream through F1.
insights.implication: Racing is the Pacers' origin story: the 1967 name nods to the Indy 500 pace car and harness-racing pacers. Get ahead of the F1-led racing trend with the bullring version: sign-painted numbers, crew jackets and clay-dust color, with no licensed IMS marks.

insights.title: Gym-hoppers are Hoosier Hysteria's own subculture
insights.detail: Indiana's giant high school gyms draw a circuit of gym-hoppers. They include New Castle's roughly 7,300-seat fieldhouse (once about 9,300) and Knightstown's Hoosier Gym, where the film's Hickory played. Hoppers photograph old gyms, thrift sectional-champion tees and letter jackets, and still resent the 1997-98 switch from one open state tournament to class basketball. Milan's 1954 title, the story behind Hoosiers, is their creed.
insights.implication: The Dec 11, 2026 NBA Cup final at Hinkle Fieldhouse, where Hoosiers filmed its title game, is the moment for sectional-tee graphics and single-class nostalgia. Keep out IHSAA marks, real school mascots and the film's Hickory branding unless licensed.

insights.title: Gen Con fills downtown in the dead season
insights.detail: Gen Con is North America's biggest tabletop-gaming convention. Since 2003 it has packed roughly 70,000 gamers, cosplayers and dice collectors into the Indiana Convention Center, Lucas Oil Stadium and downtown hotels. It runs four days around the start of August, a few blocks from the Fieldhouse. In 2015 it was the first big convention to threaten to leave over Indiana's RFRA law, which helped push lawmakers into the 'fix'.
insights.implication: Make a Pacers team-store capsule with generic polyhedral dice and stat-block graphics, with local game artists. It reaches a huge audience Nike never targets. This crowd takes civic politics seriously and knows its IP, so leave out Dungeons & Dragons and Gen Con marks.

insights.title: A mall-bred sneaker scene, split between brands
insights.detail: Finish Line was founded in Indianapolis in 1976, so the city's sneaker culture grew up mall-first and retail-literate, not boutique-led. Today the hometown star's signature shoe is Puma (Haliburton's Hali line). Nike's signature athlete in the same building is the Fever's Caitlin Clark, whose 2024 arrival filled the Fieldhouse with girls in No. 22 jerseys.
insights.implication: Run Nike's Indy sneaker story through the shared Fieldhouse: Pacers-Fever crossover drops, women's-hoops product and the Pacers' Nike uniforms. Leave Haliburton's feet out of it.

insights.title: Major Taylor, the cyclist Indianapolis pushed out
insights.detail: Marshall 'Major' Taylor, born in Indianapolis in 1878, got his nickname doing trick riding in a soldier's uniform outside the Hay & Willits bike shop. After he broke records, Indianapolis tracks barred him because he was Black. He left for Worcester, Massachusetts, and won the 1899 world sprint title. The Major Taylor Velodrome on Cold Spring Road and Marian University's championship cycling program keep track and BMX riding alive.
insights.implication: A track-jersey Pacers piece honoring Taylor is a powerful Indianapolis-only story. Make it only if it's co-created with Black cycling clubs and youth programs, names the exclusion plainly and clears his name and likeness first.

insights.title: Small, protective DIY and queer rooms
insights.detail: Saturday Punk Rock Night at the Melody Inn, all-ages hardcore at the east side's Emerson Theater, and drag and burlesque at Fountain Square's White Rabbit Cabaret form the city's DIY core. Queer Indy organizes through Indy Pride every June. The 2015 RFRA fight and recent anti-LGBTQ laws keep the community politically alert.
insights.implication: Leave the punk rooms unbranded and, at most, commission their flyer artists by name. Build Pride product with Indy Pride and local drag performers, credit and pay them, and keep proceeds local.

hoops.headline: In Indiana, basketball is a religion, and the brick fieldhouse is the church
hoops.summary: Indiana's hoops identity lives in high school gyms, the Hoosiers myth and the IU-Purdue split, with Indianapolis as the hub. The Pacers sit on top, with Tyrese Haliburton back from his Achilles tear and the Fever sharing Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Locals dress plain, in college colors and school-gym nostalgia. Honor the gym and the small-town school before the big-city streetball myth.

insights.title: The fieldhouse is the cathedral
insights.detail: Hinkle Fieldhouse at Butler, the 1954 Milan title behind the film Hoosiers and small-town gyms like New Castle's (among the largest high school gyms anywhere) anchor the state's faith. The 2026 Emirates NBA Cup final is at Hinkle on Dec 11.
insights.implication: Build a Hinkle-week capsule around brick, hardwood and rafters and banners. Make the gym, not a logo, the hero graphic.

insights.title: Crispus Attucks is a story to credit, not borrow
insights.detail: Indianapolis's Crispus Attucks High School, with Oscar Robertson, won the 1955 and 1956 state titles. It was the first all-Black school to win the tournament, in a segregated city. It is a point of pride in Black Indianapolis and a piece of civil-rights history.
insights.implication: Partner with the school, its alumni and community institutions on any Attucks product, and pay and credit them. Don't use its marks without a license.

insights.title: Two college religions, one state
insights.detail: Indiana (cream and crimson, Assembly Hall) and Purdue, in black and old gold at Mackey Arena, split the state. Butler, Notre Dame and Indiana State (Larry Bird's school) share the pride. Locals pick a side early and keep it.
insights.implication: Pacers navy and gold overlaps with Purdue's old gold, so avoid colorways that read as college product. Check licensing on any college reference.

insights.title: Mr. Basketball and the All-Star series are the local draft
insights.detail: The Indiana Mr. Basketball award and the Indiana-Kentucky All-Star series are annual rituals that locals follow like a pro draft. The state has produced Eric Gordon, Mike Conley Jr., Greg Oden and Zach Randolph.
insights.implication: Seasonal drops and player stories can draw on the Mr. Basketball lineage. Name-and-likeness uses need athlete agreements.

insights.title: Haliburton's comeback is the new local legend
insights.detail: Tyrese Haliburton returns from the Game 7 Achilles tear to lead a team coming off a 19-63 year, with Siakam, Nembhard, Nesmith and new center Ivica Zubac. Purdue point guard Braden Smith joined on a two-way deal, which ties college loyalty to the pro team.
insights.implication: Lead with resilience and return, in guard-oriented product. Treat the Purdue tie as a hometown-hoops storyline.

insights.title: Indiana is a women's basketball market too
insights.detail: The WNBA's Indiana Fever share Gainbridge Fieldhouse with the Pacers, and Caitlin Clark's arrival made them a national draw. Indiana high school girls' basketball has deep history too.
insights.implication: Plan co-ed and women's-first hoops product for Indianapolis from the start.

fanbase.headline: The Pacers belong to the whole state, and their fans can't stand hype
fanbase.summary: Hoosier Hysteria comes from Friday-night high school gyms, Indiana and Purdue, and Hinkle Fieldhouse, and Pacers fans treat the team as the one pro club the whole state shares. Reggie Miller's Knicks villainy, the ABA titles and the 2025 run to Game 7 of the Finals built the loyalty. After the 19-63 lost year, the mood is protective hope.

insights.title: Fandom is statewide and rooted in high school gyms
insights.detail: Pacers fans run from Evansville to Fort Wayne to the Region. That's because Indiana basketball starts in county-seat gyms, sectional tournaments and the Hoosiers myth, not in the NBA. A Pacers cap turns up in Milan and Marion as readily as in Indianapolis.
insights.implication: Build for the whole state, not just Indy neighborhoods. A county-gym and "Hoosier Hysteria" layer (nets, brick gyms, painted-floor graphics) will land harder than a skyline story.

insights.title: Reggie was the first myth. Haliburton is the next
insights.detail: Kids hear about Reggie's 1990s Knicks battles as scripture, including the eight points in under nine seconds in 1995. The 2025 Finals run revived that underdog swagger. Haliburton's injury in Game 7 turned admiration into protectiveness.
insights.implication: Pair a Reggie-era heritage story (1990s pinstripe-adjacent graphics, number 31 in the vault) with a Haliburton comeback story. Avoid anything that reads as a manufactured star push.

insights.title: Proud of a team the nation overlooks
insights.detail: Fans wear the chip of being overlooked by national media. The up-tempo, pass-first style Rick Carlisle coaches matches the local ideal of effort over ego. Indiana also splits its attention among the Colts, the Fever, the Indy 500 and college hoops.
insights.implication: Be earnest and hard-working, with no hype-beast posture. Craft detail, honest materials and quiet gold accents beat loud logos.

insights.title: The college-pro bridge is unusually strong
insights.detail: Purdue and Indiana loyalties are tribal, yet Pacers fans cross over. The Pacers' second-round pick of Purdue's Braden Smith is the local-hero story fans love. Butler's Hinkle Fieldhouse hosts the 2026 NBA Cup final on Dec 11, which puts the pro game inside the state's basketball cathedral.
insights.implication: Hinkle is a rare chance for a limited, place-specific drop and event. License Butler, Purdue and IU marks separately.

insights.title: Race, class and region shape who wears what
insights.detail: Indianapolis has a Black basketball culture, with courts and rec centers on the near-Eastside and Northwest side. Beside it sit rural white small-town gym tradition and a growing family base in suburban Carmel and Fishers. Each group reads the same navy and gold differently.
insights.implication: Work with Indy's Black community creators and local retailers as credited, paid authors. Don't borrow street style from outside.

insights.title: A redemption season sells
insights.detail: After a 19-63 season, demand for a healthy, Haliburton-led team will be high, and the home opener is a ritual of return. The Cup final in Indianapolis (Dec 11) adds a second local peak.
insights.implication: Time a hero release to the home opener and Cup week, not to a national calendar. The returning Moments Mixtape City Edition (white, royal blue, gold) gives you a ready canvas.

rhythm.headline: Indiana's year is basketball all the way round, with one May interruption for the 500.
rhythm.summary: Pacers fever peaks from April to June, when the playoffs collide with the Indy 500 month. Winter belongs to Hoosier Hysteria, from November to the Final Four, and the team shares it with Purdue, IU and the IHSAA tournament. The 2025 Finals heartbreak and a 19-63 year without Haliburton left a hungry base. Buying clusters around a hot start, the Cup, holiday gifts and any playoff run.

insights.title: Spring is the peak, and the 500 is the neighbor
insights.detail: In May the whole city dresses in racing graphics, checkerboard and speedway imagery, just as the playoffs overlap with the Indy 500 build-up. Fans switch between the two identities within a single week.
insights.implication: Plan a playoff-gear drop that can flex into May: navy, gold and a restrained checkered or speedway-adjacent graphic. Don't fight the 500 for attention. Make a bridge piece, not a competing one.

insights.title: Comeback narrative sets the fall launch
insights.detail: Haliburton returns from the Game 7 Achilles tear after a lost 19-63 season, alongside Siakam, Nembhard, Zubac and the 2025 Finals core. That makes October to December a redemption story. The fans who stuck through the lost year are the ones buying.
insights.implication: In Oct-Nov, lead with team-first, resilience-themed "Home" product, not generic opener merch. Add NBA-licensed jerseys once Haliburton has played at home. He is a Puma athlete, so skip signature-adjacent lifestyle product.

insights.title: The Cup final at Hinkle is the local jackpot
insights.detail: The Emirates NBA Cup final is Friday Dec 11 at Butler's Hinkle Fieldhouse, the 1928 barn tied to the Milan 1954 championship and the film Hoosiers. Indiana is also in Cup East Group B with the champion Knicks. It opens Cup play at home on Oct 30 vs the 76ers.
insights.implication: Build a Pacers-marks-only winter capsule that sells from Nov 1: brick, wood floor and arched-roof graphics in Pacers navy and gold, never Butler blue. Add a Hinkle-named layer only if Butler and the NBA clear it. Peak retail at the Dec 11 final.

insights.title: Winter belongs to college and high school hoops
insights.detail: From January to March, Purdue, IU and the IHSAA boys and girls tournaments dominate conversation, and small-town gym pride peaks. The Pacers hold their own, because Indiana fans consume all of it. Casual attention still dilutes in February.
insights.implication: Use the dead zone for community-court and gym-culture stories, not hard retail. All-Star (Feb 19-21, Phoenix) barely registers for this team unless a Pacer is selected.

insights.title: Fever summers keep the building warm
insights.detail: The Indiana Fever play in Gainbridge Fieldhouse from May to September. They have made the arena a year-round destination with a younger, more national audience. Pacers attention from June to September is thin outside the draft, free agency and Summer League.
insights.implication: Shared-city product with Indy-first graphics, not tied to one team, can ride summer foot traffic. Keep it a separate brief, with WNBA/Fever licensing handled correctly.

insights.title: No opening-night or Christmas spotlight
insights.detail: The Pacers have no opening-night or Christmas Day game, and they open the regular season after Oct 20. Their national stage comes from Cup games, Prime/NBC windows and the Presidents' Day game vs Golden State on Feb 15.
insights.implication: Don't anchor a launch on a national-TV tentpole. Anchor it on the first home game and the Oct 30 Cup night, and let a winning streak drive replenishment.

uniform.headline: Indiana's navy and gold date to the ABA, and the Pacers' own archive is still underused.
uniform.summary: The Pacers have worn blue and gold, with a grey accent, since the ABA days. Fans love the looks of Reggie Miller's 1990s and the ABA title years best, and for 2026-27 the team is reportedly bringing back its Moments Mixtape City Edition. The untold stories are the gyms and the ABA's Black stars, and the Dec 11 Cup final at Hinkle Fieldhouse is the moment to tell them.

insights.title: The palette is the state's basketball default
insights.detail: Navy and gold are Pacers colors, but Indiana high school and college gyms are also full of blue-and-gold and old-gold wood tones. So the team reads as the whole state's, not just the city's. The 1990s are the nostalgia peak for adult fans.
insights.implication: Tonal navy-and-gold product can sell statewide. Push regional retail (small-town sporting goods, Fort Wayne, Evansville, Bloomington) as well as downtown.

insights.title: Moments Mixtape is a rerun
insights.detail: The 2025-26 white, royal blue and gold City Edition is reportedly returning for 2026-27, after a 19-63 season and Haliburton's Achilles recovery. A repeat jersey lets the fan story be about the return, not a new concept.
insights.implication: Spend design energy on cassette, mixtape and playlist graphics, tees and warm-ups around the repeat jersey, not a fresh concept. Tie drops to Haliburton's comeback.

insights.title: Hinkle Fieldhouse is the 2026 brand moment
insights.detail: The Emirates NBA Cup final is Dec 11 at Butler's Hinkle Fieldhouse, the barn of the 1954 Milan story and the Hoosiers film. For a short window the NBA sits inside Indiana's gym mythology, even though the Pacers aren't guaranteed a place in the final.
insights.implication: A Hinkle-derived drop (brick, arched trusses, hickory floor graphics) timed for early December works for the Pacers and for the Cup final in general. Clear the licensing with Butler first.

insights.title: The ABA vein runs deeper than the '90s
insights.detail: The Pacers won three ABA titles (1970, 1972, 1973) with Roger Brown, Mel Daniels and George McGinnis under coach Bobby Leonard. Their blue and gold shared the stage with the league's red, white and blue ABA ball. Fans know Reggie better than the ABA, so the ABA is the more distinctive story.
insights.implication: Make an ABA-era Classic Edition capsule: Pacers blue and gold, period lettering and a restrained red, white and blue ABA-ball accent. It gives collectors something other than a 1990s repeat.

insights.title: Racing is the state's other visual religion
insights.detail: Every Indiana household shares the Indianapolis 500, the Speedway's checkered flag and its yard of bricks in May, and earlier Pacers alternates have used racing cues. The catch is that racing is also the most obvious cue.
insights.implication: Use racing with a lighter hand: brick texture, a fine flag-check pattern, pit-crew typography. Skip the literal checkered flag, which reads as a cliche.

insights.title: Attucks and the gyms, still untold on a jersey
insights.detail: Crispus Attucks High School won state titles in 1955 and 1956 with Oscar Robertson, the first all-Black school in the country to do so. Its story is separate from the Hickory and Milan myth. Statewide gym lore (New Castle, Hinkle, small-town consolidation losses) has barely reached NBA product.
insights.implication: Partner with the school and its alumni, and credit them on any apparel. Don't borrow the school's marks without permission.
